# Presentation Slides

Professional slide visuals for decks and pitches.

## Design Principles

### One Slide = One Idea
Don't combine unrelated concepts. Audiences remember 65% of what they see vs 10% of what they hear.

### Content Limits
- Max 5 bullets per slide
- 15-20 words per text block
- Heading + list OR a paragraph, not both

### Typography
```
Heading: 44-54 pt, bold
Subheading: 28-36 pt, medium
Body: 18-24 pt, regular (min 18 for readability)

Fonts: sans-serif as primary (Inter, Helvetica, Roboto)
Serif for accents only
```

### Contrast & Color
- 3-4 colors max (primary + 2-3 accents)
- One neutral background (white/black/gray)
- Contrast min 4.5:1
- Avoid pure white #fff on black - use #f5f5f5

### Whitespace
- Content needs room to breathe
- Asymmetric layouts (2/3 + 1/3) are more dynamic than centered ones
- If it's cramped - split it into two slides

### Visual Consistency
- One style: photos OR illustrations OR minimal graphics
- Mixing = visual chaos
- High-res only, every image reinforces the idea

### Checklist
```
☐ One slide = one idea
☐ Max 5 bullets
☐ Heading 44-54pt, body 18-24pt
☐ 3-4 colors, high contrast
☐ Enough whitespace
☐ High-res visuals, one consistent style
```

## Slide Types

### Hero Title (Dark)
```
Create dramatic title slide for [CONTEXT] presentation.

Background: Gradient from [DARK hex] to #0a0a0a.
Atmospheric: subtle mist at lower edge.

Typography:
"[MAIN TITLE]" in extra bold, white, extremely large, upper third
"[SUBTITLE]" in thin, muted, 5x smaller, below

Mood: Confident, premium
Format: 16:9
```

### Data Visualization
```
Create data slide for [CONTEXT] presentation.

Background: Dark gradient [hex] to [hex].

Hero number: "[METRIC]" in bold, [ACCENT], center
Trend: [up/down arrow] in [green/red]
Supporting: 3-4 smaller metrics below

Chart: [TYPE] showing [DATA]

Mood: Analytical, impactful
Format: 16:9
```

### Comparison (Light)
```
Create comparison slide for [CONTEXT].

Background: Off-white #fafafa to #f0efed.

Split layout:
Left: "[OPTION A]" with details
Right: "[OPTION B]" with details

Emphasis: Right side accent bar #3b82f6

Mood: Clear, objective
Format: 16:9
```

### Insight/Problem
```
Create insight slide for [CONTEXT].

Background: Clean off-white.

Focal: "[KEY MESSAGE]" in bold, centered
Supporting: "[CONTEXT]" smaller, below
Emphasis bar: [ACCENT] strip with data point

Mood: Clarity, focus
Format: 16:9
```

### Process/Timeline
```
Create process slide for [CONTEXT].

Flow: [HORIZONTAL/VERTICAL]
Stages: [1]→[2]→[3]→[4]
Each: icon + "[LABEL]" + description
Connectors: arrows in [ACCENT]

Format: 16:9
```

## Typography

**Hierarchy:**
- Hero: "Extremely large, dominating upper third"
- Primary: "Large, commanding"
- Secondary: "3-5x smaller than hero"
- Footer: "Minimal"

**Weight:** thin | regular | medium | bold | extra bold
**Position:** "upper third", "left aligned 10% margin", "centered"

## Color Systems

**Dark palette:**
- Near-black: #0a0a0a, #121212
- Deep tones: #0d3d2d, #1a2a3a
- Text: #ffffff, #e0e0e0

**Light palette:**
- Off-white: #fafafa, #f8f9fa
- Warm gray: #f5f5f4
- Text: #1a1a1a, #374151

**Data colors:**
- Positive: #22c55e
- Negative: #dc2626
- Highlight: #3b82f6

## Atmospheric Effects

- "Subtle gradient haze"
- "White mist at ground level"
- "Soft vignette darkening edges"
- "Noise texture for premium feel"

## Layout Systems

Universal layout rules. They work with any visual style.

---

### Bento Grid

A modular system of blocks of different sizes.

**Core Rules:**
- A parent container with clear module boundaries
- Hierarchy: important content → large blocks, secondary → small ones
- Max 9 blocks (otherwise it's overloaded)
- Uniform gaps (16px standard)
- Related content is grouped in one block

**Sizes:** wide/flat (hero) | narrow/tall (lists) | square (icons)

**Grids:**
```
3-block:           6-block:             9-block:
┌───────┬───┐     ┌───┬───┬───┐       ┌─────┬───┬───┐
│ HERO  │SEC│     │ S │ S │ S │       │HERO │MED│ S │
├───────┴───┤     ├───┴───┼───┤       ├──┬──┴───┼───┤
│  FOOTER   │     │ CHART │LST│       │S │ MED  │ S │
└───────────┘     └───────┴───┘       └──┴──────┴───┘
```

**Prompt:**
```
Layout: bento grid, [N] blocks
Hero block: [MAIN], Medium: [SECONDARY], Small: [ICONS]
Gaps: uniform spacing
```

---

### Asymmetric Grid

Dynamic compositions with visual balance.

**Rules:**
- Start with a base grid, then break it deliberately
- Balance weight: one large element on the left = several small ones on the right
- Rule of Thirds for natural balance
- Emphasize key elements through size and position

**Use for:** creative presentations, portfolios, fashion, startups
**DON'T use for:** banks, government portals, data-heavy B2B, older audiences

**Prompt:**
```
Layout: asymmetric composition
Left: [LARGE - 60%], Right: [2-3 SMALLER stacked]
Balance: visual weight distributed
Rule of thirds positioning
```

---

### Negative Space

Space as a tool for focus.

**Rules:**
- It structures, rather than creating emptiness for the sake of looks
- It directs attention and focuses on what matters
- Gestalt: elements with space between them = separate, close together = related

**Use for:** premium brands, minimalist presentations, hero sections
**DON'T use for:** news portals, dashboards, mobile versions

**Prompt:**
```
Layout: generous whitespace
Focal point: [ELEMENT] with breathing room
Empty space: intentional, guides eye to [CTA]
```

---

### Split Screen

A two-column composition.

**Proportions:**
- 50/50 - equally weighted elements
- 60/40 - emphasis on one side
- 70/30 - clear hero + support

**Prompt:**
```
Layout: split-screen [RATIO]
Left: [CONTENT], Right: [CONTENT]
Divider: [sharp / gradient / none]
```

---

### Brutalist

Raw aesthetics, huge type, bright colors.

**Rules:**
- Keep navigation and hierarchy clear
- Readability > expression
- Apply selectively: bright colors OR huge type

**Use for:** artist portfolios, fashion, startups
**DON'T use for:** e-commerce, corporate, education, fintech

**Prompt:**
```
Style: brutalist design
Typography: massive, raw
Colors: high contrast, bold
Hierarchy: clear despite unconventional styling
```

---

## Futuristic / SaaS Style

Apple Keynote minimalism + glassmorphism + 3D objects.

### Visual Language
```
Style: Apple Keynote + SaaS + glassmorphism
Mood: premium, immersive, clean, breathable
Lighting: volumetric, ray-traced reflections, ambient occlusion
Base: deep void black OR pure ceramic white
Accents: aurora gradients (neon purple, electric blue, coral, cyan)
```

### Glassmorphism Cards
```
Material: frosted glass with blur
Edges: delicate white borders
Shadow: soft, diffused
Spacing: generous internal whitespace
```

### 3D Visual Anchors
```
Purpose: abstract 3D artifacts as focal points
Materials: polished metal, iridescent acrylic, transparent glass, soft silicone
Shapes: capsules, spheres, shields, Möbius strips, fluid waves
Quality: looks like expensive collectibles
```

### Composition by Type

**Cover:** huge 3D glass object center + bold title + aurora background
**Content:** bento grid + 3D icons in small cards + text in large cards  
**Data:** split-screen (text left, glowing 3D chart right)

### Charts Style
```
3D donut charts, glowing
Capsule-shaped progress bars
Floating numbers with neon glow
Style: looks like glowing neon toys
```

### Example Prompt
```
Create a futuristic SaaS slide for product presentation.

Style: Apple Keynote + glassmorphism.
Mood: premium, immersive, clean.
Background: void black with aurora gradient (purple → cyan).

Layout: bento grid, 6 blocks.
Cards: frosted glass, blur, white edges, soft shadows.
Hero block: floating iridescent sphere.
Data blocks: glowing 3D donut chart, neon metrics.

Typography: clean sans-serif, high contrast white.
Format: 16:9
```

## Named Deck Styles

Ready-made combinations of "background + accent + typography + image treatment". The palettes above give colors separately; a named style is a finished package: pick one, apply it to the whole deck, don't mix. One accent per deck, not two.

### Dark Cinematic — the default when the topic doesn't suggest a style

- **Background:** deep graphite or dark navy #121212 → #0a0a0a toward the edges, barely visible grain.
- **Accent:** electric blue #3b82f6 **or** warm gold #d4a24a. One of the two, not both.
- **Secondary tone:** ivory #f5f1e8 for text.
- **Typography:** a dense modern grotesque for headings, large slide numbers.
- **Images:** a cropped hero with a gradient mask, blended into the slide rather than dropped in as a rectangle.
- **For:** strategy, premium brands, editorial breakdowns, executive talks.

### Dark Sports

- **Background:** near-black #0a0a0a with a light gradient from the top, a light vignette.
- **Accent:** red #ef4444; data and callouts in cyan #22d3ee.
- **Typography:** a bold condensed grotesque, italic allowed; large numbers in the style of jersey numbers.
- **Images:** high-contrast action photography, blown-out stadium lights as glow, tightly cropped portraits.
- **For:** sports recaps, match breakdowns, esports, any topic with scores and tables.

### Dark Analytical

- **Background:** graphite with a barely visible map or coordinate grid.
- **Accent:** amber #f59e0b; routes, connections and data labels in cyan #06b6d4.
- **Typography:** a calm editorial grotesque plus a monospace for numeric labels.
- **Images:** full-slide maps under a dark overlay, satellite imagery, connection lines.
- **For:** news analysis, logistics and supply chains, market breakdowns, briefings.

### Dark Editorial

- **Background:** near-black, flat, no gradients.
- **Accent:** warm gold #d4a24a **or** coral #f87171 — one.
- **Typography:** serif headings, a quiet grotesque for body text. The feel of a long-form magazine feature.
- **Images:** one hero per slide, beautifully cropped, minimal overlays — the photo does the work.
- **For:** journalism, documentary topics, brand storytelling.

### Dark Luxury

- **Background:** pure black, perfectly flat.
- **Accent:** gold leaf #c9a961, in literally just a few places.
- **Secondary tone:** muted ivory #f5f1e8.
- **Typography:** high-contrast serif headings, wide tracking, a clean grotesque for body text.
- **Images:** minimal. B&W or duotone, one object per slide.
- **For:** luxury, watches and jewelry, private banking, investment stories.

### Light Minimal

- **Background:** warm white #fafaf8, lots of air.
- **Accent:** exactly one color matched to the brand or topic; only for headings, dividers and one highlight per slide.
- **Secondary tone:** gray #9ca3af for secondary text.
- **Typography:** serif **or** geometric grotesque — pick one direction and stick with it. Large type size, generous leading.
- **Images:** a clean cropped photo with no overlays, with proportional margins.
- **For:** B2B and SaaS, design-driven brands, talks, conference keynotes.

### Light Commercial

- **Background:** white or full-slide blocks of the brand color.
- **Accent:** a saturated brand color (cobalt, scarlet, electric green) matched to the product itself.
- **Typography:** bold grotesque, heavy weights, product-first presentation.
- **Images:** large product shots, high key, clean shadows, colored blocks behind the object; charts directly in the brand color.
- **For:** consumer product launches, retail, mass-market campaigns, agency pitches.

### Glass SaaS

No separate description needed — it's the **Futuristic / SaaS Style** section above: aurora gradients, frosted-glass cards, 3D anchors. This style fits AI, tech and creative agencies.

### How to choose

- Sports, news, geopolitics → dark sports or dark analytical.
- Strategy, brand, documentary → dark cinematic, editorial or luxury.
- AI, SaaS, creative agency → glass SaaS.
- B2B, expertise, design brand → light minimal.
- Consumer goods and retail → light commercial.
- Topic doesn't suggest a style → dark cinematic.

Tell the user the chosen style before generating — it's cheaper to ask again than to regenerate the deck.

> **Hypothesis, not a verified fact:** there's an observation that GPT Image tends to underexpose slides in dark styles. If that holds for your task, explicitly ask for high contrast and well-developed highlights on the main object. This behavior hasn't been measured in our sources.

---

## Building a Six-Slide Deck

When you need not one slide but an overview board (six 16:9 tiles in one image — patterns in [multi-panel.md](multi-panel.md)), layouts are chosen not by taste but to fit the narrative arc.

- **Open and close deliberately.** The first slide is a Hero Title, the last is a closing slide: one line of takeaway, optionally a call to action and a signature. The closing slide echoes the language of the first, but quieter: same palette and typography, calmer composition. Don't recap the deck's content on it.
- **Don't put two slides of the same type in a row**, and don't use any type more than once per six slides. Two identical layouts side by side read as a layout mistake.
- **Alternate density.** A text slide is followed by a visually dominant one. Four text slides in a row kill the board.
- **Topic with numbers** → at least one slide where the hero is a number or a chart (Data Visualization above) is required.
- **Topic about a person** → a portrait slide: the portrait takes about half the area, next to it the name, role and two or three facts in small type.
- **Controversial or comparative topic** → Comparison. Three entities instead of two is no longer a comparison but a set of cards.
- **Chronological topic** → Process/Timeline, 3-5 nodes. Eight nodes on one slide are unreadable.
- **A strong thesis or the client's voice** → a quote slide: a large line, attribution below it, a quiet background.
- **The accent is applied the same way** on all six: if you decided the accent colors the headings and one number, do that on every slide. Inconsistent accent use breaks a deck apart more than different layouts do.
